topics.title: 36.1 mmap
topics.summary: mmap requests a mapping with a length, protection flags, sharing mode, descriptor, and offset. Failure is reported as MAP_FAILED , not as a null pointer. A zero-length mapping is not a valid substitute for handling an empty file. The offset must satisfy the platform’s alignment requirements, normally a multiple of the relevant page size. Mapping an arbitrary record offset often requires rounding the mapping base down to a page boundary and retaining an internal displacement, with overflow checks on the total mapped length.

topics.title: 36.2 Address mappings
topics.summary: The returned address identifies the beginning of the mapping in the process’s virtual space. Its validity lasts until the mapping is removed or otherwise changed. Closing the original descriptor does not by itself remove an established mapping on Linux. Pointers into the region become invalid after munmap . A function borrowing the mapping must not retain those pointers beyond the owner’s lifetime. Mapping ownership deserves the same discipline as allocation ownership: one clear owner, explicit extent, and structured cleanup.

topics.title: 36.3 File-backed pages
topics.summary: File-backed pages associate virtual regions with file contents. A shared writable mapping can propagate modifications to the underlying file according to synchronization and filesystem rules. A private mapping provides private modification semantics instead of updating the file with those writes. Mapping flags are not a complete interprocess synchronization protocol. Multiple writers need an agreed layout and synchronization mechanism. Data-race rules still apply to threads in one process, and process-shared synchronization requires facilities designed for that purpose.

topics.title: 36.4 Page faults
topics.summary: The first access to a mapped page may fault so that the kernel can establish backing. Later accesses can still fault under memory-management activity. A mapping therefore does not promise that every load has register-like or even DRAM-like cost. Concurrent file truncation is a serious hazard. Accessing a mapped region whose backing has been removed can generate SIGBUS on Linux. Checking file size before mapping is not enough when another actor can shrink the file afterward. The example below requires a stable regular file throughout the mapping’s lifetime.

topics.title: 36.5 Mapping permissions
topics.summary: Protection flags specify permitted reads, writes, and instruction execution. They must be compatible with the mapping and descriptor’s access rights. A read-only mapping is appropriate for a checksum or parser that does not need to modify the file. Use the least authority required. Do not request writable executable memory merely because it seems convenient. For writable shared file mappings, msync can request synchronization under its documented semantics, while a complete durable-update protocol may require additional filesystem operations. [ R31 , R32 , R33 ]

topics.title: 36.6 Memory-mapped I/O
topics.summary: The phrase memory-mapped I/O also describes device registers placed in an address map. Device mappings are not ordinary file-data mappings: accesses can have side effects, supported widths, ordering requirements, and cacheability constraints. A volatile pointer alone does not provide every device-ordering or synchronization guarantee. Device access must follow the operating system’s driver interfaces and architecture-specific requirements. This book’s user-space file-mapping labs do not access physical device registers.

LECTURE NARRATION
A memory mapping exposes a file region through virtual addresses. The program accesses bytes with ordinary loads and stores, while the kernel supplies backing pages and enforces mapping permissions.
